rationale: Placed after the 'Principles of Regional Anaesthesia' block to reinforce the mechanism of action of local anaesthetics before moving to indications.
Placed after the subarachnoid and epidural spaces anatomy block to test understanding of the key anatomical distinction — a classic AS examination trap.
Placed after the pharmacology block to apply knowledge of maximum LA doses — a critical safety calculation tested in AS examinations.
Placed after the clinical indications block to consolidate understanding of when peripheral nerve blocks are preferred over general anaesthesia.
Placed after the brachial plexus techniques block to distinguish the four approaches — a commonly tested topic in regional anaesthesia.
Placed after the monitoring and interpretation block to reinforce recognition of local anaesthetic systemic toxicity (LAST) — a life-threatening emergency.
Placed after the sacrum and sacral hiatus anatomy block to test recall of the key landmark — the foundation for safe caudal technique.
Placed after the paediatric caudal technique block to apply the Armitage formula — the most clinically important dose calculation for paediatric caudal block.
Placed after the adult caudal technique block to address the key anatomical reason why the adult technique is more technically challenging than the paediatric approach.
